text: Some companies pushed their prices up further than their own costs went up, and pocketed all the difference as record profit.
When only a handful of companies sell a thing, they can keep the price up, since nobody else is undercutting them.
Shipping and materials got dearer, and firms passed that on to shoppers, and some of them passed on more than that.
Inflation means the same money buys less than it used to, so a price that stays still is really going down.
When more people want a thing than there is of it, its price climbs until fewer people are willing to pay.
The government borrowed and spent a great deal, and that put more money into people's hands chasing all the same goods.
Government spending was a big cause: more money going round with no more things to buy means every price ends higher.
The central bank held rates near zero for years and made new money, which cuts what each dollar is really worth.
Sunlight looks white, but it is really every colour mixed up together, which is just what you see in a rainbow.
At sunset the light comes in low through much more air, the blue is scattered away, and red is left over.
Near the horizon the sky looks paler, because the light there came in through more air and bounced about more times.
There is no air in space, so there is nothing to scatter the sunlight and the sky there is simply black.
Air is made of molecules far too small to see, and the light coming down from the sun bumps into them.
So the blue light ends up scattered right across the whole sky, and that scattered blue is what you look at.
Blue light travels in shorter waves than red light does, and the shorter a wave is the more easily it scatters.
Violet waves are shorter again than blue ones, but our eyes are much less sensitive to violet, so we see blue.
